title: Philippines Sends BRP Malabrigo, BRP Teresa Magbanua on Resupply Run to BRP Sierra Madre at Ayungin Shoal
detail: The Philippines conducted a rotation-and-resupply (RORE) mission to its military outpost aboard the grounded BRP Sierra Madre at Second Thomas (Ayungin) Shoal on August 22, 2026, deploying the 44-meter Philippine Coast Guard vessel BRP Malabrigo and the 97-meter BRP Teresa Magbanua — the PCG's longest-deployed West Philippine Sea asset — according to monitoring by the maritime transparency initiative SeaLight. The PCG vessels were closely shadowed throughout by China Coast Guard and maritime militia ships, a now-routine pattern under the 'provisional understanding' President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has confirmed exists with Beijing over resupply notifications, which he has said does not amount to seeking China's permission or conceding sovereignty. The mission came about five weeks after the July 20, 2026 clash near the shoal in which Chinese coast guard personnel allegedly boarded Philippine boats and struck a Filipino Navy sailor with a metal rod, and follows the Philippine DFA's August 11 statement that 15 RORE missions had by then been completed under the arrangement without incident.

media.caption: BRP Malabrigo and BRP Teresa Magbanua sailed on a resupply run to BRP Sierra Madre at Ayungin Shoal, shadowed by China Coast Guard and militia vessels
